title: Field Survey Photo Verification for Crop Insurance
summary: Check geotagged field survey photos for crop insurance claims for location, timing, crop type, visible damage and reuse, so claim officers spend their time on cases that need judgement.

seo.title: Crop Insurance Field Photo Verification | VipraTech
seo.description: AI checks of geotagged crop insurance survey photos for location, timing, crop type, visible damage and photo reuse, with claim officers deciding.

problem.intro: Crop insurance claims for localised calamities and post-harvest losses depend on field surveys, crop cutting experiments and the photos surveyors upload from the field. In a bad season, thousands of photos arrive within a few weeks, and claim teams cannot check every one for location, timing or reuse.

pain_points.title: Photos that do not match the plot
pain_points.detail: Geotags fall outside the insured survey number, or the photo shows a different crop from the one declared at sowing.

pain_points.title: Reused and recycled images
pain_points.detail: The same photo, or a near-copy, appears across several claims or comes from a previous season.

pain_points.title: Timing gaps
pain_points.detail: Photos taken before the reported event or long after harvest weaken the evidence but are hard to spot manually.

pain_points.title: Survey backlog during calamities
pain_points.detail: After heavy rain, hail or a pest outbreak, claim teams face a spike in surveys with fixed reporting timelines.

solution.overview: We build a verification layer that checks every survey photo and its metadata before a claim officer opens the file. It compares the photo's geotag with the plot boundary or survey number on record, checks the timestamp against the reported loss event and crop calendar, and confirms the visible crop matches the sowing declaration. A vision model describes visible damage such as lodging, waterlogging or pest attack, without estimating a payable loss. Perceptual hashing finds reused or near-duplicate photos across claims and seasons. Survey forms are read so their details can be compared with the photos. Each claim gets a checklist of passed and failed checks, and failed or uncertain items go to a claim officer.
capabilities: Geotag check against plot boundary or survey number coordinates
Timestamp check against the reported event date and crop calendar
Crop type recognition compared with the sowing declaration
Visible damage description such as lodging, waterlogging or pest attack
Duplicate and near-duplicate photo detection across claims and seasons
Per-claim evidence checklist for claim officers

workflow.title: Receive the survey packet
workflow.detail: Photos, metadata and survey forms arrive from the surveyor app or survey agency upload, grouped by claim or intimation number.

workflow.title: Check location and time
workflow.detail: Geotags and timestamps are compared with the insured plot and the reported loss event.

workflow.title: Check crop and damage
workflow.detail: The vision model confirms the crop type and describes visible damage in standard categories.

workflow.title: Check for reuse
workflow.detail: Each photo is compared with earlier photos across claims and seasons to find copies and near-copies.

workflow.title: Route by result
workflow.detail: Claims where all checks pass go forward; failed or uncertain checks go to a claim officer or for re-survey.

workflow.title: Officer decision and record
workflow.detail: The claim officer decides with the checklist and photos in front of them, and the decision and evidence are logged.

inputs: Geotagged survey and crop cutting experiment photos
Survey forms and claim intimation details
Insured plot details with survey or khasra numbers
Reported loss event dates and affected areas
outputs: Per-claim verification checklist with pass, fail or uncertain status
Flags for location, timing, crop mismatch and photo reuse
human_in_the_loop: Claim officers and surveyors decide every claim. The system checks evidence and describes visible damage, but it never estimates payable loss or rejects a claim on its own; failed checks lead to review or re-survey, not automatic denial.
integrations: Surveyor mobile app or survey agency portal
Land record and plot boundary data, where available
National Crop Insurance Portal data exports, where available
guardrails: No automatic claim rejection from any single check
GPS drift tolerances agreed with the claims team
Original files kept unchanged, with checks run on copies
Farmer identity and location data restricted by role
Regular sampling of passed claims by a senior claims officer
compliance_notes: Designed to support the photo, geotag and survey evidence practices described in PMFBY operational guidelines, without replacing the surveyor's assessment.
Claim records and audit trails help insurers evidence fair claim handling under IRDAI expectations.

pilot.scope: Photos from one completed season's surveys in one or two districts, re-checked against decisions already made, before any use on live claims.
deliverables: Check rules agreed with your claims team
Verification pipeline run on historic survey photos
Report comparing flags raised with past decisions
Plan for live use in the next season

what_we_measure.how: Share of flags that claim officers agree are genuine issues on review.
Count of reused or near-duplicate photos detected and confirmed by manual check.
Model crop type compared with the sowing declaration and the officer's judgement.
Time to review a claim with and without the checklist, measured on a sample.

faqs.q: Can this decide how much crop was lost?
faqs.a: No. It checks whether the photo evidence is consistent and describes visible damage. Loss assessment stays with surveyors, crop cutting experiments and the claim officer.

faqs.q: What if GPS is inaccurate in the field?
faqs.a: Phone GPS can drift, so the location check uses tolerances agreed with your team and treats small deviations as uncertain rather than failed. Officers see the distance on a map before deciding.

faqs.q: Does it work with photos from different surveyor apps?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as photos keep their metadata or the app records location and time separately. If metadata has been stripped, the system flags the photo so it can be retaken.
Data stays in your cloud or an India region, access is restricted by role, and only the fields needed for verification are processed. Original files are never modified.
